# Data

<!-- Describe input coverage, exclusions, units, and source versions with inline R. -->

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
dt <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds"))
diagnostics_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compile-diagnostics.rds")
diagnostics <- if (file.exists(diagnostics_path)) readRDS(diagnostics_path) else NULL
metadata_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compile-metadata.rds")
metadata <- if (file.exists(metadata_path)) readRDS(metadata_path) else list(data_downloaded_at_label = "Not recorded")
individual_metadata <- if (!is.null(diagnostics) && !is.null(diagnostics$individual_metadata)) {
  diagnostics$individual_metadata
} else {
  list(n_records = NA_integer_, n_stations = NA_integer_, n_observed_weights = NA_integer_)
}
station_n <- nrow(dt)
positive_station_n <- sum(dt$rho_biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
zero_station_n <- sum(dt$rho_biomass == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
year_n <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$startyear)
survey_n <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$missionid)
```

This document and the associated analyses are based on [index-wise](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/index-wise) and were developed with researcher-supervised generative AI.

The compiled dataset was extracted from the IMR Biotic database on `r metadata$data_downloaded_at_label`.

# Analysis

## Data collation

The station catch data and individual fish measurements are acquired from the IMR Biotic database when the survey-selection document is compiled. Survey selection qualifies individual surveys first and then retains all valid hauls from qualifying surveys so true-zero hauls remain available. This report reads the compiled station dataset and compiler diagnostics; raw individual-level records are used for length allocation but are not written to the project.

The compiled dataset uses station-level catches for the complete haul roster and individual-level length measurements for the length products. The generic data flow is:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-data-schematic
%%| fig-cap: "Generic data collation workflow. Quality-filtered station catches provide the haul roster; individual lengths are combined with length-weight allocation and rescaling to produce total and length-specific biomass products."
flowchart LR
  A[IMR Biotic station catches] --> B[Station and region filters]
  B --> C[Compiled station dataset]
  D[IMR Biotic individual lengths] --> E[Length and quality filters]
  E --> F[Compiled individual dataset]
  C --> G[Length-weight allocation]
  F --> G
  C --> H[Total biomass]
  G --> I[Biomass at or below threshold]
  G --> J[Biomass above threshold]
```

### Station-level data

The station-level dataset has one row per retained bottom-trawl haul after the configured gear, mission, distance, station-type, sample-quality, year, and exact-region filters. Target-species catch records are aggregated over catch samples within a haul. The compiler first builds the station roster independently of target catch weight. If no target-species catch row is present after the standard haul and region filters, its biomass is set to zero and the haul is retained as a true zero. If a target catch row is present but any target catch weight is missing, or the summed catch count is less than the summed length-sample count, or the summed catch weight is less than the summed length-sample weight, the haul is excluded and recorded in the catch-quality audit; it is not converted to zero. The primary station-level observation retained for modelling is raw target catch weight (`biomass`, kg). The compiler also derives swept-area biomass density (`rho_biomass`) for descriptive checks by dividing catch weight by swept area. For a catch-weight formulation, use `biomass` as the response and pass `log(swept_area_nmi2)` to `sdmTMB::sdmTMB()` through its `offset` argument. This keeps zero-catch hauls in the data while scaling the positive catch process to the sampled area. In a delta family, the sdmTMB offset applies only to the positive component, so document and validate separately whether swept area also enters the occurrence component. Gear type can remain a fixed effect when a common width is used across different trawls.

### Individual-level data

The individual-level dataset is filtered to target-species records from the qualifying surveys and retained haul roster. Duplicate specimens are removed using haul, catch-sample, and specimen identifiers. Lengths are converted to centimetres. In subsampled catches, each measured fish is represented by the recorded haul count divided by the number of measured fish; unavailable counts default to one.

## Length-based data

Length-based products combine the station-level total catch with individual-level length composition. Use observed individual weights where available and estimate missing weights from a documented length-weight relationship. For measurement $i$, multiply estimated weight $w_i$ by its superindividual representation $s_i$, calculate the share of each length group from the resulting weights, and rescale those shares to the recorded station biomass. Thus, for group $g$, $B_g = B \times (\sum_{i \in g} w_i s_i / \sum_i w_i s_i)$. State the threshold, whether the threshold belongs to the lower or upper group, and how positive hauls without usable lengths are handled. The length-specific products should sum to total biomass whenever usable length information exists.

The overview below is generated from the compiled objects rather than hard-coded counts. If the compiler records individual-level metadata, report the number of length records and stations here as well.

## Overview

The station-level dataset contains `r format(station_n, big.mark = " ")` retained hauls from `r min(dt$startyear)` to `r max(dt$startyear)` across `r format(year_n, big.mark = " ")` years and `r format(survey_n, big.mark = " ")` qualifying surveys. `r format(positive_station_n, big.mark = " ")` hauls are target-positive and `r format(zero_station_n, big.mark = " ")` are true-zero hauls. The intermediate individual dataset contains `r format(individual_metadata$n_records, big.mark = " ")` length records from `r format(individual_metadata$n_stations, big.mark = " ")` stations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-report-overview
knitr::kable(
  dt |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      `Stations` = format(dplyr::n(), big.mark = " "),
      `Years` = paste0(min(startyear), "–", max(startyear)),
      `Cruise series` = format(dplyr::n_distinct(cruiseseries), big.mark = " "),
      `Positive stations` = format(sum(rho_biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = " "),
      `Zero stations (%)` = round(100 * mean(rho_biomass == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
    ),
  caption = "Overview of the compiled {{SPECIES_NAME}} {{REGION_SLUG}} station dataset."
)
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding and refer to @tbl-data-report-overview. Confirm caption units, sample size, and interval definitions against the generated result. -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-report-survey-response-table
knitr::kable(
  dt |>
    dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      hauls = dplyr::n(),
      positive_hauls = sum(rho_biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      zero_fraction = mean(rho_biomass == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_positive_density = median(rho_biomass[rho_biomass > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  caption = "Station-level response summaries by cruise series."
)
```

## Station positions

```{r station-map}
#| fig-cap: "Final retained station positions in the {{REGION_SLUG}} prediction region. Points distinguish true-zero and positive target-species hauls."
sp <- dt |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(longitudestart), !is.na(latitudestart))
ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = sp, bathymetry = TRUE, bathy.style = "rbg") +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = sp,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = longitudestart,
      y = latitudestart,
      colour = rho_biomass > 0
    ),
    size = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "grey65", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
    labels = c(`FALSE` = "True zero", `TRUE` = "Positive"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
```

## Sampling through time and depth

```{r}
#| label: fig-data-report-annual-stations
#| fig-cap: "Number of retained hauls by year and cruise series, separated into target-positive and true-zero hauls."
dt |>
  dplyr::count(startyear, cruiseseries, caught = rho_biomass > 0) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(startyear, n, fill = caught)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cruiseseries, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Year", y = "Retained hauls", fill = "Target caught")
```

```{r}
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey45", colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Bottom depth (m)", y = "Retained hauls")
```

## Response distribution

```{r}
#| label: fig-data-report-response
#| fig-cap: "Positive swept-area density distribution for the compiled target species. The x-axis is logarithmic; true-zero hauls are retained in the compiled dataset."
dt |>
  dplyr::filter(rho_biomass > 0) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(rho_biomass)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Positive biomass density", y = "Positive hauls")
```
